input.quote: 22.14 Solicitation. Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
input.rationale: Section 22.14 bars us (and M&I) from soliciting any employee of the other party, for any reason, for the whole multi-year Term. That fails the fallback on scope (all employees rather than personnel directly involved in the Services), duration (the entire Term rather than 12 months from the end of involvement) and carve-outs (none for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches). The redline keeps the clause mutual and no-hire-free, changes only the duration words in the existing sentence, and adds one sentence supplying the scope limiter and the two carve-outs, landing the clause at the fallback.

mappings.element: Non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services.
Non-solicit limited to 12 months from the end of their involvement.

ops.oldText: 22.14 Solicitation. Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
ops.newText: 22.14 Solicitation. Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during and for 12 months from the end of their involvement.

ops.text: The preceding sentence applies only to employees directly involved in the performance or receipt of the Services, and does not restrict general advertisements or other general solicitations not specifically directed at the other party's employees, or unsolicited approaches by an employee of the other party.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the open-ended Term-long bar with a restriction running only during, and for 12 months from the end of, the relevant employee's involvement, and added one sentence confining it to employees directly involved in the Services with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.
proposal.summary: Narrow mutual non-solicit to involved personnel for 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs
